- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 30d mean), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- Model exhibits strong lag in reacting to sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns negative after 3–5 days, forecast should be adjusted downward by 0.3–0.8% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30d horizon, model often underestimates true volatility; apply a 0.2–0.5% upward bias if sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67) over last 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (neutral or bearish), model tends to underestimate; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to avoid “bearish trap” bias.
